title: Zesty Vietnamese Rice Vermicelli Banh Mi
description: A charred, creamy Vietnamese banh mi filled with seasoned tofu, spicy rice vermicelli, and fresh herbs.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and slice baguette lengthwise, leaving the ends connected.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on the cut side of the baguette and roast on a baking sheet for 5 minutes until lightly charred.
Press tofu between paper towels, cut into 2 cm cubes, and season with soy sauce, maple syrup, and sesame oil.
Cook the seasoned tofu in a hot skillet over medium-high until all sides are golden and slightly crispy, about 8 minutes.
Boil rice vermicelli in salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Toss vermicelli with sriracha and a pinch of salt to coat evenly.
Combine the cooked vermicelli with shredded carrots, sliced cucumber, and chopped cilantro in a bowl.
Slice the roasted baguette into 2 cm thick slices and spread a thin layer of lime juice on each slice.
Spoon the vermicelli mixture onto the baguette slices, drizzle with a little extra sesame oil, and sprinkle with optional toasted sesame seeds.
Fold the baguette halves together, slice into individual servings, and garnish with lime wedges before serving immediately.
